issues.title: Direct malloc instead of zmalloc
issues.description: The rule requires using zmalloc() wrapper for memory allocation, but malloc() was used directly in the cluster initialization code
issues.rule_name: Use zmalloc/zfree Wrappers Instead of Direct malloc/free

issues.title: Incorrect operation order causes potential data loss during cluster verification
issues.description: The verifyClusterConfigWithData() function executes clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots() before clusterClaimUnassignedSlots(). This reverses the intended logic: the function should first claim ownership of unassigned slots that contain keys (preventing orphaned data), then delete keys from slots that are genuinely owned by other nodes. With this bug, keys in unassigned slots may be incorrectly deleted before the node has a chance to claim ownership, resulting in permanent data loss during cluster startup or recovery scenarios.

issues.title: ASM cron runs before cluster state update causing stale state issues
issues.description: The serverCron() function now calls asmCron() before clusterCron(). This is problematic because clusterCron() contains the call to clusterUpdateState() which updates the cluster's operational state (CLUSTER_OK vs CLUSTER_FAIL). ASM (Atomic Slot Migration) operations depend on having an accurate view of the cluster state to make correct migration decisions. By executing asmCron() first, migration tasks may operate on stale cluster state information from the previous iteration, potentially leading to incorrect slot migration decisions, failed migrations, or data consistency issues during cluster rebalancing operations.

issues.title: Internal helper function clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots missing static declaration
issues.description: The function clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots() is defined and used only within cluster.c (no external callers, not declared in any header file), but lacks the 'static' keyword. According to AGENTS.md Rule #7, all internal helper functions that are not part of the public API must be declared static to enforce proper encapsulation and prevent symbol pollution. This violation could lead to naming conflicts in large codebases and breaks the repository's explicit encapsulation requirements.

issues.title: Non-static internal helper function exported from cluster.c
issues.description: `clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots()` is introduced as a file-local helper and is only used within `src/cluster.c` (called by `verifyClusterConfigWithData()`), but it is declared without `static`, unnecessarily exporting the symbol outside this compilation unit. Per the rule, internal helper functions must be declared `static`.
issues.rule_name: Rule 7: Internal Helper Functions Must Be Declared Static

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14587 - Refactor some of ASM and slot-stats functions

structured_output.summary:
The PR claims to be a pure refactor. It moves verifyClusterConfigWithData() from cluster_legacy.c into cluster.c and splits it into two helpers, clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots() and clusterClaimUnassignedSlots(). It also moves asmInit/asmCron/asmBeforeSleep and the slot-stats allocation into a new clusterCommonInit() called from main(), and relocates the CLUSTER MIGRATION and CLUSTER SYNCSLOTS dispatch from clusterCommandSpecial() into clusterCommand().

Most of the relocation is sound. The ASM cron and before-sleep hooks keep their cadence and cluster-enabled gating, and the command dispatch is equivalent. The verification split is not behavior-preserving, though. The new delete pass runs before the claim pass and treats unowned slots as foreign, so keys in slots that nobody owns are deleted instead of claimed. That is a data-loss regression on restart. The PR description says there are no behavioral changes, and that is not true.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The split of verifyClusterConfigWithData() has a correctness bug that can silently drop keys on startup. clusterIsMySlot() is false for a NULL owner, and getImportingSlotSource() is NULL for unowned slots. So clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots() deletes keys in unowned slots before clusterClaimUnassignedSlots() gets a chance to take them. The original code claimed those slots. Swapping the call order fixes it. The malloc-vs-zmalloc change for cluster_slot_stats is a smaller issue but should also be addressed before merge.

architecture.overview:
Redis cluster startup runs through main() in server.c. When cluster is enabled, main() allocates the per-slot stats array and calls clusterInit(), which sets up the cluster state and the ASM (atomic slot migration) manager. Later, verifyClusterConfigWithData() reconciles keys loaded from disk with the slot table. Periodic work runs from serverCron() (clusterCron and, now, asmCron) and beforeSleep() (clusterBeforeSleep and, now, asmBeforeSleep).

This PR does three things. It moves the startup-time reconciliation out of cluster_legacy.c into the shared cluster.c and splits it into two helpers, one that deletes keys in slots owned by others and one that claims slots with keys that have no owner. It moves asmInit() and the slot-stats allocation into a new clusterCommonInit() called from main() before clusterInit(). It also moves the ASM cron and before-sleep hooks out of the legacy clusterCron()/clusterBeforeSleep() and into server.c, and moves CLUSTER MIGRATION and CLUSTER SYNCSLOTS dispatch up into clusterCommand().
steps: Entry point: main() in server.c. When cluster is enabled it now calls clusterCommonInit() (stats and asmInit) and then clusterInit(), replacing the direct zmalloc of cluster_slot_stats.
Periodic and before-sleep hooks: serverCron() and beforeSleep() in server.c now call asmCron() and asmBeforeSleep() directly next to the legacy cluster hooks.

Startup reconciliation: verifyClusterConfigWithData() in cluster.c first runs clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots() and then clusterClaimUnassignedSlots(). The claim helper lives in cluster_legacy.c and is the only mechanism-specific piece.

Ordering is the risk point: the delete pass treats any slot that is not mine and not importing as foreign, which includes slots with no owner. Those keys are dropped before the claim pass can adopt them.
Command routing: CLUSTER MIGRATION and CLUSTER SYNCSLOTS are now matched in clusterCommand() ahead of clusterCommandSpecial(). The behavior is the same.

findings.title: Unowned-slot keys are deleted before they can be claimed
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/cluster.c`, `verifyClusterConfigWithData()` (around lines 2208-2213) calls `clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots()` before `clusterClaimUnassignedSlots()`. Because `clusterIsMySlot()` is false for NULL-owned slots, the delete pass drops keys in unowned slots that the claim pass should adopt. Swap the two calls so the claim runs first. Also make sure `clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots()` (lines 2146-2169) only deletes keys in slots that have an owner that is not `myself` and is not importing, for example by checking `getNodeBySlot(i) != NULL`. Keep the original behavior: unowned populated slots are claimed, not deleted. Do not change the cluster_legacy.c claim logic.

findings.title: cluster_slot_stats switched from zmalloc to unchecked malloc
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/cluster.c`, `clusterCommonInit()` (around line 2138) allocates `server.cluster_slot_stats` with `malloc()`. Change it back to `zmalloc()` to match the previous allocation in `main()` in `src/server.c` (around line 7739) and the rest of the codebase's allocator use, so the memory is counted in `zmalloc_used_memory()`. Do not change the rest of the initialization order.

findings.title: Startup ordering moves ASM and stats init ahead of clusterInit
findings.body: `clusterCommonInit()` now calls `resetClusterStats()` and `asmInit()` before `clusterInit()` builds `server.cluster`. I checked the current code and both are safe in that order. `resetClusterStats()` only checks `server.cluster_enabled` and `memset`s the stats array, and `asmInit()` does not touch `server.cluster`. The dependency is implicit, though. A future change to `asmInit()` that reads cluster state would break this quietly. A short comment in `clusterCommonInit()` stating that it must run before `clusterInit()` and must not depend on `server.cluster` would help.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/cluster.c`, add a comment to `clusterCommonInit()` (around line 2137) saying it runs before `clusterInit()` and therefore must not read `server.cluster`. Note that it resets slot stats and initializes ASM. This documents the ordering dependency that `main()` in `src/server.c` (around line 7739) relies on.

findings.title: ASM cron and before-sleep relocated with unchanged behavior
findings.body: Moving `asmCron()` out of `clusterCron()` and into `serverCron()`, and `asmBeforeSleep()` out of `clusterBeforeSleep()` and into `beforeSleep()`, keeps the same cadence and the same cluster-enabled gating. Both hooks are still called only when `server.cluster_enabled` is set, and `asmBeforeSleep()` still runs after the cluster before-sleep work. The `CLUSTER MIGRATION` and `CLUSTER SYNCSLOTS` dispatch moves from `clusterCommandSpecial()` into `clusterCommand()`, which is the only caller of `clusterCommandSpecial()`, so the routing is equivalent. The split of the `clusterCommonInit()` and `clusterInit()` calls also keeps the ASM manager initialized before any command or cron can use it.
